summary: Specializing in history, archaeology, and Indology, Michael Jansen studied at Bonn, RWTH Aachen (earning his Promotion), Rome, and Delhi. He served as Dean of the Faculty of Architecture at RWTH Aachen (1988–1999) and founding rector of GUtech (2007–2008).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Michael Jay Sweet earned his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, also studying under Geshe Wangyal and Richard Robinson. He held clinical assistant professorships in psychiatry at Wisconsin-Madison.

Michael Jerryson specialized in Buddhist and religious studies. After undergraduate studies at Wisconsin-Madison, he earned his PhD at UC Santa Barbara under Mark Juergensmeyer. He taught at Eckerd College (~2009–2012) and Youngstown State University (~2012–2021).
Michael Kowalewski works in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.

Michael L. Walter worked in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, having studied under Larry William Moses. He was a research fellow at the Lumbini International Research Institute (attested 2000) and special languages cataloger at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2020).
Michael M. Broido specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge and later held a post at the University of Oxford.
Working in Tibetology and related fields, Michael Oppitz held an appointment at the Institute for Advanced Study, Berlin (~1987–1988) and served as director at the University of Zurich (~1991–2008).
Michael P. Berman works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. By 2012, he was attested as a professor at Brock University and as managing editor of the Canadian Journal of Buddhist Studies.

Michael Puett is a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Marshall Sahlins and Anthony C. Yu. He has held professorships at Harvard University, including the Walter C. Klein Professorship.

Michael Pye studied at Cambridge and Leeds (Ph.D.) and worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He held lectureships at Leeds and Lancaster, a professorship at the University of Marburg (1982–2004), and a visiting professorship at Otani University.

Michael R. Sheehy works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD from CIIS under Steven D. Goodman. He held posts at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center and the University of Virginia (attested 2019–2026).

Michael Radich, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and computational methods, completed his PhD at Harvard under Robert M. Gimello. He held posts at Victoria University of Wellington (2005–2017) and became Professor of Buddhist Studies at Heidelberg University in 2018.
Michael S. Drummond specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies from the University of Bristol and was attested as a PhD candidate at Utrecht University in 2006.

Michael Schmidt worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as a dictionary editor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 1981) and held posts at the KOHD (1992) and the University of Göttingen (attested 1995).

Linguist Michael Silverstein completed his education at Stuyvesant High School and Harvard University (~1961–1971). He subsequently served on the faculty at the University of Chicago from around 1971 until 2020.

Michael Stanley-Baker works in Sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology, having earned an MA at Indiana University Bloomington under Stephen R. Bokenkamp. He has held posts at MPIWG, University of Leipzig, University of Pittsburgh, and Nanyang Technological University.
Michael Torsten Much is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Ernst Steinkellner and was a fellow at the University of Hamburg.

Michael Viggo Fausbøll was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Niels Ludvig Westergaard at the University of Copenhagen. He worked at the University of Copenhagen as an assistant librarian (1861) and later Professor of Indian Philology (1878–1902).

Michael W. Meister specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his BA, MA, and PhD at Harvard University and also studied at the University of Pennsylvania, where he became a professor around 1976, succeeding Stella Kramrisch.

Michael Weiers studied at the University of Bonn, completing his dissertation around 1965. A specialist in Iranian, Central Asian studies, and linguistics, he served as professor at Bonn (1972–2003) and honorary professor at Inner Mongolia University.
